note: Item codes are the SPSS column names in the study's own data file and data/niazi_2020_moral_foundations.py melts them through unchanged (var_name='item', no prefix for this table; the STP_-prefixed twin becomes niazi_2020_mfq_stereotype), so there is no rename and no positional step. That .sav (PLOS S1 Data, pone.0229926.s002) labels all 32 MFQ columns with their statements, which is what ties code to text (mapping_basis=data_labels). DEVIATION, disclosed: item_text is NOT those labels but the canonical MFQ30 wording from moralfoundations.org/wp-content/uploads/files/MFQ30.doc (full version, July 2008, Graham, Haidt & Nosek), because the .sav labels are the depositor's abridgement -- Part 1 labels drop the instrument's 'Whether or not ' lead-in (e.g. 'someone suffered emotionally') and two carry scoring annotations ('someone was good at math[use this to cut if >2]', 'It is better to do good than to do bad[use this to cut if <3]'). The paper states it administered exactly that source: 'The English version of the Moral Foundations Questionnaire by Graham, et al., (referred to as MFQ30) was used, which is a 30 item, close-ended questionnaire that was last revised in July 2008 and is freely available at moralfoundations.org.' Labels reconcile to the shipped text 32/32 after stripping the lead-in, the bracketed annotations and punctuation (see verify_niazi_2020_mfq.R). Administered in English (inclusion criteria required 'ability to read, understand and write English'), so no language/_translated columns. Two section_ids because the two MFQ30 parts have different anchors: part1 'moral relevance' 0=not at all relevant..5=extremely relevant, part2 'moral judgement' 0=Strongly disagree..5=Strongly agree, both as printed in MFQ30.doc; instructions left empty since the only framing text is per-part and belongs in section_prompt. MATH (part 1) and GOOD (part 2) are the MFQ30's two catch items, shipped as items because the IRW table stores them as items; they are not scored into any foundation. No correct_response (no key). RIGHTS: no restriction found and none quotable. The moralfoundations.org questionnaires page distributes MFQ30.doc with 'If you are a researcher and you want to collect data yourself, please use the MFQ30' and states no fee, no permission requirement, no non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution term; MFQ30.doc itself carries only the attribution line 'The Moral Foundations Questionnaire (full version, July 2008) by Jesse Graham, Jonathan Haidt, and Brian Nosek.' The page's footer '(c) Copyright 2024 by MoralFoundations.org. All rights reserved.' is a bare copyright notice, not a clause reserving a right, and the instrument has no row in itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv. Silence is permission, so it ships. Step 3b: live data is 32 items x resp 0-5 matching the MFQ30's 30 items plus 2 catch items and the paper's 0-5 six-point scales; the sibling table niazi_2020_mfq_stereotype holds the same 32 statements rated for a typical member of the other gender.
